customer: I'm trying to sell my electric car and just found out my mom's name is on the title too, and she's working out of state right now. I'm a full-time student in California and can't keep rescheduling my appraisal over paperwork. Do I really need her there, or can I just sign for both of us?
agent: I understand the frustration, and I'm glad to help you sort this out quickly. Per our article "When more than one person owns the car," it depends on how the names appear on the title: if they're joined by "or," only one owner needs to sign, but if they're joined by "and," every owner has to sign. If your mom's signature is needed and she can't attend the appraisal, she can sign a power of attorney, form NW-POA-1, which must be notarized. Otherwise, the easiest route is for all owners to come to the appointment with their photo IDs.
